title: Hierarchical abstractions as a basis for ontology graphs
summary: Compiled and reviewed the branded 20-page LaTeX white paper: 22 cited sources, three propositions, software counterexamples, reproducible finite checks and synthetic results. Citation/build/layout checks pass; reusable workflow isolation and rollback tests pass.

events.summary: Research protocol defined. Starting the primary-source literature review.
Scope, evidence criteria, public progress page and two-minute ntfy/publishing automation are established. Reviewing primary sources next.
Direction confirmed: theoretical foundations for software-engineering micro-agents, authored by Out of Distribution Labs. Reusable project workflow extracted; primary-source review continues.

Reviewed 22 primary sources across abstraction, ontology semantics, software contracts, graph retrieval, coordination and distributed state; recorded access limits and pinned source versions. Beginning formal synthesis.

Formalized contextual abstraction domains, task-relative sufficiency, typed polyhierarchies and claim admission. Added proofs of composition/separation and counterexamples for summary loss and inconsistent distributed merges.

Ran reproducible routing simulations for 100, 300 and 1,000 logical workers across 20 seeds. Complete hierarchy matches a strong flat index; missing cross-module memberships reduce recall and guarded fallback increases cost. These are synthetic structural results, not LLM performance claims.

Synthetic evaluation complete: 100, 300 and 1,000 logical workers, 20 seeds and overlap/coverage stress tests. Complete hierarchy matches flat indexing; omissions lose recall and coverage fallback raises cost. No LLM or patch-success claim.
